scoringRule: Each assistant contributes one scored outcome per task. Completed purchases take precedence over unsuccessful attempts.

methods.goal: Can an AI assistant turn a shopping request into an accepted order—and what happens when checkout, payment or delivery gets in the way?
methods.login: On open-choice tasks, we directed assistants toward guest checkout when sign-in blocked progress.
methods.scope: 25 assistants, eight shopping tasks each, 200 scored outcomes. Six tasks specified the retailer; two let the assistant choose the store.
methods.timing: Elapsed time runs from the request to confirmation and includes approval waits. Agent working time subtracts time waiting for tester replies.
methods.acceptance: Accepted means an order was placed and was not cancelled by the merchant at the payment stage.
methods.human: Payment setup, approval and card entry could require tester input. Dazzle uses human-assisted checkout rather than browser automation, so its result represents a different completion route.

taskBriefs.prompt: Help me buy one new Logitech M170 wireless mouse, black, with its USB receiver, from Amazon. Deliver to same address. Confirm the cart before you checkout.

methods.intro: We gave 25 assistants eight shopping tasks each: six at named retailers and two where they chose the store. We asked them to confirm the cart before checkout, then recorded order acceptance, cancellations and what arrived.

findings.billing: When using a new credit card, the agents used the shipping address as the billing address without asking the user to confirm it. Dick’s cancelled both orders because the addresses did not match the card’s billing details.
